QF.id: XIII Introduction to the Underlying Markets_58

question.text: What is 'Holding Period Return' (HPR) of a bond?

answer.text: The total realised return earned over the holding period, including coupon receipts, reinvestment income where applicable, and any price/redemption gain or loss
The coupon rate of the bond multiplied by the holding period
The return earned only from reinvesting coupon payments
The yield to maturity of the bond at the time of purchase

explanation.text: The Logic: HPR is computed ex post, once the actual reinvestment rates and the realised price/redemption outcome are known. Bond returns over a holding period combine periodic coupon income, reinvestment income on those coupons and capital gain or loss on price/redemption. The Trap: Reducing HPR to a simple coupon-plus-price-change formula understates the reinvestment-income component and ignores that HPR is realised, not projected. YTM, in contrast, is an expected return that assumes reinvestment at the YTM itself. Note: Because reinvestment outcomes are only knowable after the fact, HPR cannot be quoted with certainty in advance; it is calculated once the holding period is complete.
